subject: Google Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, published 2026-09-02
central_claim: Gemini 3.8 Flash is a publishable AI engineering topic because Google and Google DeepMind primary sources support a bounded E2/R1 claim: the release moves the Flash line toward long-horizon software engineering and agent workflows with model ID gemini-3.8-flash, 1M input context, 64K output, tunable low/medium/high thinking levels, built-in agent tools, Antigravity default usage and documented pricing, while benchmark superiority remains vendor-authored and is not promoted to an independent ranking conclusion.

selection.reason: Gemini 3.8 Flash is a September 2026 production model release with multiple official primary sources: announcement, model card, API docs, pricing and evaluation methodology. It was reviewed but not selected on 2026-09-12 because Claude Fable 5.1 had a sharper immediate migration contract; for 2026-09-13 it remains a distinct unmaterialized topic because GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 have already been covered and Gemini 3.8 Flash changes the Flash model line's role in long-horizon agent and coding workloads. The conclusion is bounded because no API call, benchmark rerun or independent evaluation was performed.

claims.claim: Google released Gemini 3.8 Flash as a production Gemini API model for long-horizon software engineering and agent workflows, with inspectable API documentation for model ID, context, output limit, thinking levels, tool support, Antigravity default use and pricing; the publishable conclusion is about the documented engineering contract, not independently verified benchmark superiority.

Opened Google's September 2 announcement for Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber. Opened the Gemini model family page. It lists Gemini 3.8 Flash as the current workhorse model for complex agentic tasks and links to model details, safety, performance and ecosystem sections.

Opened the Gemini API latest-model page. It documents model ID gemini-3.8-flash, GA status, 1M context, 64K output, low/medium/high thinking levels, unsupported minimal level, Antigravity default use and introductory pricing.

Opened the Gemini API model page. It documents stable model ID, input and output limits, modalities, supported tools, computer use preview, batch/flex/priority consumption options and September 2026 latest update.

Opened the Google DeepMind model card. It confirms publication on 2026-09-02, links the model to Gemini 3.7 Flash, states input/output scope, distribution channels, benchmark result table, known limitations, safety regression note for non-English languages and Frontier Safety assessment.

Opened the evaluation methodology PDF. It explains pass@1 settings, self-computed Gemini results, provider self-reported non-Gemini numbers, public leaderboard usage and benchmark-specific notes for DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench, OSWorld, HLE-Verified and related evaluations.
Opened Gemini Developer API pricing. It documents Standard, Batch, Flex and Priority pricing for Gemini 3.8 Flash, context caching prices and the January 1, 2027 standard-pricing transition.

Recent visible items included Qwen3-VL and older Qwen image/safety/model-family posts; no accessible same-day model/API/runtime candidate with stronger SW-engineering decision value than Gemini 3.8 Flash was confirmed in this pass.

Reviewed DeepSeek official GitHub and Hugging Face registry start points for same-week release signals. The recent DeepSeek V4.1-Flash path had already been considered in prior AI runs, and no fresher primary-source-backed topic outranked Gemini 3.8 Flash for this publication date.

Opened Mistral home and documentation surfaces. Signals included Mistral OCR 4/4.1, Vibe, AI Cloud and model-list updates. These were relevant but either narrower document-intelligence or platform announcements, and did not exceed Gemini 3.8 Flash's model/API/evaluation package for the AI판's regular article.
